newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes weaker, prompt Minas depressed.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes weaker, prompt Minas depressed.

text.p: Asian crude values weakened further on Tuesday following the overnight fall in futures, traders said..
Prompt availabilities of Minas also kept the June heavy sweet crude market depressed, although traders expected July to be stronger, with deals already done at premiums over the ICP.
In late Asia trading on Tuesday, the overnight drop in crude futures steadied, with Simex front month Brent last traded at 17.60 for July, up 4 cents per barrel from London close.
Paper Tapis responded to the overnight fall in crude futures, with July offered at 19.75, compared to 19.80/95 discussed on Monday.

On the physical market, there were distressed sellers of June Minas, although July trading have started, traders said. A Widuri seller recently sold some July barrels above ICP +10, a contrast to a June Minas trade done Friday at ICP -20, they said.
Minas and Widuri usually trade at similar levels.
Chinese demand for July heavy sweet crudes remained unseen, but there was enough Japanese enquiries to support the market at premiums between 10-15, traders said.
But there were worries that the narrow Brent/Dubai spread could revive Asian refiners' interest in West African crudes, which will compete with regional grades.
The Middle East crude market was steady, with most of the July supplies committed.
The last Oman trades were heard done Friday at MPM -30, but with only limited supplies left, discounts were not expected to deepen.
